text:
alex: Starting handoff now. Quick heads-up: I'm moving primary to maria. Leaving behind two notes: 1) We have an SLO alert noise spike for inference-latency P95 in us-west-2 — it started ~30m ago and is trending up. 2) I temporarily bumped the alert threshold to avoid paging during the maintenance window (details below). If it looks customer impacting, escalate immediately.

incident-bot: ALERT: service=inference-latency environment=prod region=us-west-2 metric=P95 value=620ms threshold=500ms state=ALERTING (fired at 1769000900).

maria: ack — thanks. Can you paste the exact threshold change commands and link to the runbook? Also what's the expected degradation (if any) for customer requests? :eyes: 

alex: pasted below. Expected customer impact: most tail latency is background (batching backlog) but some interactive requests may see >500ms P95. No 5xx spike yet. No active support tickets.

alex: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency
Commands (internal alert manager):
```
/alerts set-threshold --service=inference-latency --env=prod --region=us-west-2 --metric=P95 --value=700ms --reason="maintenance window, will revert after handoff"
/alerts annotate --id=ALERT-1769000900 --note="temp threshold bump during infra work; contact oncall if customer-facing errors appear"
/alerts mute --id=ALERT-1769000900 --duration=2h
```
Use those only if you want to avoid noisy pages. I already applied the first and annotation at 1769001002.

sam: Quick Q — who's secondary for the next 4h? There's a coverage gap from 02:00-04:00 UTC where infra rotation is short. If we don't have someone, consider paging platform-oncall instead of primary-secondary.

jordan: oncall-rotation bot posted the schedule 10m ago. Copying: Primary: maria (1769001234-1769008434), Secondary: sam (1769004834-1769012034), Tertiary: platform-oncall. There is indeed a 02:00-03:00 UTC mismatch with daylight savings and EU coverage.

oncall-rotation: SCHEDULE: maria (primary), sam (secondary), platform-oncall (tertiary). Add manual escalation to platform-oncall for any service degradation during 02:00-03:00 UTC.

maria: I can take primary now. I'll confirm by running the sanity checks in runbook and subscribe to the alert channel. If the P95 keeps rising and we see error-rate >0.5% then I'll escalate.

alex: thanks — couple of pointers in the runbook under "During handoff":
- Check /metrics/p95 and /metrics/5xx for the last 15m
- If 5xx > 0.5% or latency >= 800ms P95 for >10m, escalate to platform-oncall and notify CS
- Use the rollback plan: switch to model-variant=stable-1 (see deploy commands below)

Deploy rollback command (internal deploybot):
```
/deploy rollback --service=inference --model=stable-1 --region=us-west-2 --reason="latency mitigation"
```

maria: running sanity checks now. result: P95 = 640ms (15m avg), 5xx = 0.08%. I'll keep monitoring; not yet customer impacting per thresholds but we should watch.

sam: I'll cover the 02:00-03:00 UTC gap — can take secondary earlier if needed. If you want me to be on immediate page, say so.

maria: please stand by as backup, thanks. If I need escalation I'll ping platform-oncall and add them to the incident thread.

jordan: small ops suggestion — set a temporary alert policy that pages only after a sustained 10m window to reduce churn during draining/eviction periods. Example policy snippet in alert-manager:
```
- alert: HighInferenceLatency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.8
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
This reduces immediate pages for short-lived spikes.

alex: noted. I configured the 'for: 10m' on the infra side already for this signal at 1769001100. That buys us breathing room.

maria: update: P95 has been flat for 5m now at ~630ms. No new customer tickets. I removed the temporary mute on the alert (so we still get alerted if it crosses the higher threshold again) but left the threshold at 700ms until the handoff completes.

sam: if it crosses 800ms and 5xx creeps, I'll trigger the rollback. Do we want to notify affected customers preemptively? We have no active tickets but we might proactively message top tier customers.

alex: agree — prepare templated note (short) to send to top 5 customers if we hit the 800ms+ & 5xx>0.5% condition. Template link: https://redwood.internal/templates/customer-notify-latency. Add CS to the thread when you send.

maria: will do. I'm taking over now. Summary for the next shift: primary=maria, secondary=sam, temp threshold=700ms in us-west-2, alert 'for' window=10m, rollback plan=stable-1 deploy. Escalate to platform-oncall if 5xx>0.5% or P95>=800ms sustained 10m.

alex: perfect. Leaving a final note in the runbook and closing my handoff. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: handoff recorded by alex -> maria at 1769001234.

maria: thanks — will update this thread if anything changes.

jordan: added a quick post-handoff checklist: confirm threshold revert after 4h, verify rollback didn't trigger incorrectly, and file a short postmortem if we had sustained degradation.

maria: copy — I'll revert threshold at 1769004834 if everything is stable and post a short summary to #incidents.

sam: :thumbsup:
